title: Epochal Slotted Lease Router and Soft-Rejection Protocol for Dedicated Fleets
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Implement a hybrid admission/routing mechanism for Dedicated fleets that provides predictable tenant throughput guarantees while enabling graceful overload handling. The core idea is an epochal slotted lease allocator: each tenant receives short-lived 'slots' (lease tokens) in fixed epochs. Slots are consumed by requests; unused slots expire at epoch boundary. On overload, the router uses a soft-rejection protocol (informative 429 + fallback routing hints + optional queued handoff) rather than hard drops to improve overall application availability and observability. This ticket covers design, prototype, load-testing, API surface, and integration with Dedicated autoscaler and Console dashboards.
acceptance_criteria: Router issues epochal leases to tenants with configurable epoch length and slots per epoch
Requests consume slots atomically; over-slot requests follow soft-rejection path with Retry-After and fallback hint header
Integration with autoscaler: slot consumption patterns feed predictor to scale pools proactively
End-to-end latency p50 remains within 1.25x baseline for steady loads with no packet loss
In load tests at 2x provisioned traffic, system yields graceful degradation with prioritized tenants kept above configured min-throughput
Console surface shows per-tenant slot utilization, epoch oversubscription heatmap, and recent soft-rejects with sample traces

technical_decisions: Use epochal slots rather than continuous token-bucket to simplify global coordination and autoscaler signals
Leases are short-lived (default 5s epoch) to bound staleness and make autoscaler signals timely
Per-pool epoch alignment chosen to avoid cross-region clock skew and reduce cross-pool coordination
Handoff strategy: when possible, router will include a signed handoff token to allow immediate retry on a fallback pool without requiring client re-auth
Lease tokens are HMAC-signed by pool key (KMS) to prevent fabric-level forgery; verification is cheap and cached
Autoscaler integration: slot-utilization metrics exposed as rolling 1m/5m/15m windows; autoscaler predictor consumes these streams

Queueing: short in-memory micro-queues per-tenant are used only when epoch slots are nearly exhausted to reduce client-facing 429s; queues have per-tenant max depth and timeouts to bound latency and memory
alternatives_considered: Global token-bucket with central coordinator: rejected due to coordination latency and scaling concerns
Per-tenant long-lived reservations: rejected because long reservations increase fragmentation and reduce autoscaler responsiveness
Immediate hard-drop (existing approach): simple but causes poor app-level availability and loss of observability into graceful fallbacks
Predictive pre-warming of slots based on workload history: viable as follow-up but deferred due to complexity
performance_expectations: Target steady-state p50 latency increase <= 25% vs current baseline for identical provisioning
Target p95 impact under overload: maintain configured min-throughput for priority tenants and soft-reject remainder
Metric: slot-utilization ratio, soft-reject-rate, fallback-success-rate, epoch-churn-rate
Soak test target: 48h stability on dedicated-qa pool with sustained 1.8x traffic spike
open_risks: Lease signing adds CPU overhead when traffic is extremely high; need microbenchmarks on verification path
Per-pool epoch misalignment during autoscaler scale events may cause transient oversubscription
Client adoption burden: clients must implement soft-retry semantics for fallback hints; need SDK updates
Edge case: tenant with very bursty short requests could starve others within epoch; need fairness adjustments and emergency demotion policy
